description: Young bear 100yds north of Michigan Camp
Yearling bear eating on beach within sight of Michigan Camp. Would not move for 45 minutes.  Group of 7 yelling and making a racket.
Bear with cub seen at bottom of ladder south of Klanawa.
Sea Lion washed ashore at camp
Bear south side of bridge 14
Bear walking the beach near Michigan
Saw a black bear somewhere between 48 km to 50 km on the beach on July 31 at 4:52 pm.
Lots of grey whale activity off shore at Michigan campsite
Downed tree blocking path at KM40 has been removed by Ditidaht trail crews.
Missing rung
Mama bear and cub at 28km, popped out on beach and back into grass
Forest trail has a fallen tree blocking the path.
Dead Sea lion washed ashore
Carmanah cable car repaired! Parks Canada trail crews replaced the damaged pull rope. The cable car is now back in service.
Helicopter currently out here fixing the cable car. Line down.
One rung is missing the middle of the ladder

In these rains the path is unclear as you head up to highest point. It looked like many people have gone off path many times before and the actual path hard to find when saturated by downpours. This app was essential in these rainy conditionss.
Cribs creek swollen with rain - waist high rushing water.
Darling River Unpassable July 26
Many whales
From the red chairs, whales and dolphins can be seen feeding.
3 different whales spotted
Small bear on the beach. Ran off into the forest when it saw us.
Single rung still missing towards the bottom
July 18 @ 9am Black Bear on trail. Spooked easily with whistle and headed into the forest.
All campsites have mice, campers found mice in their bags left outside and squirming under tents.
Bear in area around creek and beach near camp
The ladder to the toilet is missing two rungs and the toilet door is completely off the hinges
Bear seen near the entrance to the forest trail.

If camping by the river at Walbran be mindful of the high spring tide! The river’s water level rose dramatically overnight - we didn’t get wet but we came close. Might be better to camp in forest or up the beach if possible.
Nytom will likely be closed until July 20th due to access issues preventing resupply.

Rope appears damaged and cable car stuck on north. Tried multiple times including
 strong people.  Could not get it moved.

Bear approached our campsite on the south side of Michigan River last night. We spoke loudly to each other, and he walked away up stream after a short
 time.
Lone wolf at the trailhead 6:00 am July 12, observed from banks of the river opposite.
7:30 pm one bear on the beach
Lots of hiker garbage throughout the camp… hidden under logs, left in campfire rings, in the bear bins… DO BETTER FELLOW HIKERS!
One of the composting toilets is out of commission and unusable leaving only one toilet for the entire camp.
Rope on cable car has a rip and is very sponge like and is very heavy
One outhouse out of commission.  Only one composting toilet for the entire camp.
Young bear hanging around Darling Camp. Doesn’t seem interested in people
The southbound trail to Gordon river just to be really aware that the trail is not visibly clear and after crossing the creek, just follow the broken bridge to uphill
Be very mindful in the cable cars with your backpacks and gear. A croc got caught on one of the cables as we started to move over the river and severed the strap and we lost it.
Mama bear and 2 cubs crossed the trail at kilometre three
Haul rope on the Carmanah cable car damaged/frayed and looks ready to break with much more use. Cable still looks good.
one rung is missing
Beautiful colony of sea lions out on sea lion rock today!!!!
At 21km on the beach between Trestle and Klanawa - washed up dead young humpback whale. No predators seen in the area. No smell yet as it must be very recent.
Navigable bar makes cable car unnessecary. But cable cars are fun so I still did it.
Bear at 19:30 on the beach
Whales close to rock shelf at Darling in afternoon!
One rung missing, 1/3 of the way up
Look up before pitching your tent. There is a “widow maker” branch hanging in the center of the forest sites.
Sow on beach with cub at 9:30 PM.
Tons of whales today at Klanawa
A bear at darling river June 19th at 6 am.
Whale past the hole in the wall 🤩🫶🏼
Whales spouting at Clo-oose! Take a well earned break and watch the whales feed and play :) !
Two bears seen on beach headed northbound towards Darling
Km 32.4 June 10 @ 1pm. Bear on the trail 100 meters before getting to the boat (going south).
Bear on beach, not moving away from groups
We saw a bear with 2 cubs at km 72
One bear on South side of camp 2:45pm
Km 13 small black bear
Sea lion carcass on the beach at Carmanah & no one was camping there when we passed by. Thought safer to not stick around that area
Bear walking past campsite, eating something on the beach. Sunset.

Going southbound the trail is not marked visibly after the river crossing, multiple paths lead to nowhere for a few hundred meters. The actual trail goes uphill to meet back up with the path from the broken bridge.
Cheewhat South Trail ladder is missing a single rung about 2/3 of the way up.
Bear hanging around camp, strolling north along the coast
Bear strolled beach by Klanawa camp heading south, swam across and vanished into the bushes.

Some genius took a dump and left it together with a mountain of toilet paper on the access trail to the reliable water source at Klanawa on the south side by the cable car. I would avoid this water. 

For now - water can be found between the cable car and beach access on south side. It looks like a murky pond with a lot of foam from the boardwalk but if you bushwack upstream 20 ft there is a nice clean trickle. I think this is seasonal so might not be there in summer months.
Bridge 66 looks like it's missing 2 of the 3 support beams, 1 of them likely will fail soon. no easy way around either
KM71 Ladder missing a rung in the middle.
Km73 ladder with four rungs missing has been repaired by guardians. Only missing the very bottom rung which was 6” off the ground so not a problem anymore.
2 bears hanging out at Darling this afternoon and into the evening. Focused on high tide line above the mouth of the river (north side).
The 13 rung ladder segment at the KM73 gully is missing the bottommost rung, making it a big step up/down from the platform.
Forest route between Tsocowis and Darling has not been brushed yet this season.  Trail is visible but crowded by foliage.
Multiple missing ladder rungs in this section, 4 on one ladder making it very difficult to pass. Use caution especially going down!!
Was able to cross Klanawa river without the cable car at the mouth of the river at low tide.
Small black bear foraging in the intertidal zone between Darling and Michigan. We gave him lots of space and he watched us pass by before resuming foraging on the beach.
The trail was mostly dry, offering summer-like conditions. However, there were some mud bogs between the 65 km and 64 km marks.
